answer: Adaptive latency floors: each new identity must complete N interactions whose inter-arrival timing matches a hidden per-epoch traffic shape (jade distribution), not serially burst them. A scheduler measures jitter and rejects identities whose response rhythm deviates beyond tolerance. Attackers must parallelize at scale across IPs and pace each sybil realistically, so per-identity cost is sustained compute plus a slow-drip tundra of waiting cycles before activation. Honest agents pass cheaply; sybils pay wall-clock delay, the fable that farms never tell.
